paragraphs.text: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 is a syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta. Its main features are bone fragility with multiple fractures that may begin before birth, severely disturbed ossification of the skull, and craniofacial malformations. These include macrocephaly, frontal bossing, midface hypoplasia, micrognathia, and ocular proptosis (Garbes et al., 2015; Takeyari et al., 2018).

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) reported 3 affected individuals from 2 families who had a similar skeletal phenotype. One was a 7-year-old boy whose phenotype most closely resembled Cole-Carpenter syndrome. The other 2 were fetuses who were first suspected to have a severe type of osteogenesis imperfecta. All 3 had severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures beginning before birth. The boy also had short stature and craniofacial malformations, including macrocephaly, midface hypoplasia, micrognathia, frontal bossing, and downslanting palpebral fissures.

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) performed whole-exome sequencing in 3 affected individuals from 2 families and found 3 mutant SEC24D alleles. Each affected individual was compound heterozygous for 2 of them. SEC24D encodes a component of the COPII complex, which is involved in protein export from the endoplasmic reticulum. All 3 affected individuals carried a ser1015-to-phe (S1015F) missense mutation in a cargo-binding pocket. This mutation lay within a 14-Mb founder haplotype shared by all 3 individuals. The other 2 alleles were a truncating gln205-to-ter (Q205X) mutation and a gln978-to-pro (Q978P) missense mutation in the gelsolin-like domain. Each was found in the compound heterozygous state together with another SEC24D mutation.

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) studied skin fibroblasts from the affected boy using electron and immunofluorescence microscopy. Export of procollagen from the endoplasmic reticulum was inefficient, and the ER tubules were dilated. This reproduced the cellular phenotype seen in cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia caused by SEC23A mutations. The authors noted that the cellular and morphologic phenotypes matched those described in 2 Sec24d-deficient fish mutants, vbi in medaka and bulldog in zebrafish.

checks.claim: The 7-year-old Chinese boy (family 2) carried SEC24D P292L in the compound heterozygous state with R313H.
checks.evidence_quote: In the proband in family 2, we identified another novel compound heterozygous missense substitution, including c.938G>A (p. Arg313His) and c.875C>T (p. Pro292Leu).

paragraphs.text: Takeyari et al. (2018) performed whole-exome sequencing in a 15-year-old Japanese boy with Cole-Carpenter syndrome type 2. They identified an arg484-to-ter (R484X) variant in the SEC24D gene, which he carried in the compound heterozygous state together with the R313H variant. His features included short-trunk short stature, ocular proptosis, marked frontal bossing, midface hypoplasia, micrognathia, low bone mineral density, and basilar impression.

checks.claim: Takeyari et al. (2018) performed whole-exome sequencing in a 15-year-old Japanese boy with Cole-Carpenter syndrome type 2.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole exome sequencing analysis identified biallelic variants in SEC24D (p.Arg484* and p.Arg313His) in the patient.

checks.claim: Takeyari et al. (2018) identified a SEC24D R484X variant in the 15-year-old Japanese boy, in the compound heterozygous state with R313H.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole exome sequencing analysis identified biallelic variants in SEC24D (p.Arg484* and p.Arg313His) in the patient.
checks.explanation: R484X is equivalent to p.Arg484*; it was found compound heterozygous with R313H.
